results.evidence: moveToDraft calls hogFlowsPartialUpdate(status:'draft') and hydrates, so wizard becomes editable (isReadOnly = status !== 'draft'). But whether the scheduled send stops while draft depends on backend (not shown); the patch only changes status. Likely the scheduler only fires for active flows, but no scheduler code shown.

`canMoveToDraft = broadcast?.status === 'active' && batchJobs.length === 0 && !batchJobsLoading` does not check that a pending schedule exists (broadcast.schedules); an active broadcast with no batch jobs and no schedule would show it, and a completed one-time schedule with no job... Not checked against schedule state.

Old schedules are destroyed only after `hogFlowsPartialUpdate(status:'active')`, and existingScheduleIds is taken from `saved.schedules` at save time. Creation of the new schedule follows. Deletion happens for both cases, so mostly right, but existingScheduleIds is empty when broadcast was newly created, fine; however the ids come from the save response which may be stale/pause state; also Promise.all deletions. Ordering places replacement after activation, and exactly-one guarantee isn't ensured on failure. Weak; treated as not fully met.

`activated = await hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, broadcastId, { status: 'active' })` runs before `hogFlowsSchedulesDestroy` and schedule creation, so the broadcast is marked live before replacement completes (the catch reverts to draft, but the ordering is the opposite of the criterion).
Only checks batchJobs.length === 0 and !batchJobsLoading. No check of schedule count > 1 or workflow shape being wizard-editable. Batch job history unknown is covered, but not the other conditions.
Button onClick={moveToDraft} dispatches directly; no confirmation dialog.
moveToDraft only patches status to draft with a single success toast; no cancellation of started runs or warning variants.
No scheduler/backend changes in the patch.
New schedule is built only from rrule, starts_at, timezone; no variables carried over from the destroyed schedule.

result:
A live scheduled broadcast can now be moved back to draft from its summary page, and launching now replaces any existing schedule instead of reusing it. I haven't run typecheck, kea typegen or any tests, and I added no tests.

- **Move to draft:** The summary page shows a "Move to draft" button when the broadcast is active and has no send runs yet. It sets the status to `draft`, and the scene swaps to the wizard so the broadcast can be edited and relaunched. The button is disabled while the request is in flight, and a failure shows an error toast. This is a new `moveToDraft` action in `broadcastWizardLogic.ts`, with the button in `BroadcastSummary.tsx`.
- **Relaunch fix:** After launch activates the broadcast, it deletes the schedules the broadcast already had and creates a fresh one, which is always active. This also applies to the "send now" case, where any old schedule is removed. That fixes the paused-schedule case: the audience edit pauses the old schedule when the draft is saved, and the schedule's status can't be changed through the API. The new schedule is created after the old ones are deleted, so a relaunched broadcast can no longer show "Broadcast scheduled" while sitting paused.

I hand-edited the kea-typegen block at the top of `broadcastWizardLogic.ts` for the new action and reducer, since typegen wasn't run here. It will need a regenerate.
